features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education the letter cites as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct design or architecture responsibility for agent-based systems with explicit boundaries, supervision, or control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering improvements or redesigns.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, guardrails, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Collaboration posture
features.description: Captures humility, coachability, and readiness to work closely with security specialists or other experts.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers succeed through safer defaults, usable tooling, and reduced friction.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: Captures emphasis on correctness, testing, disciplined implementation, and reliability in security-sensitive engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No concrete quality practices or reliability standards are shown.
Uses generic language about rigor, seriousness, or quality.
Gives at least one clear sign of disciplined implementation, such as typed or tested code or production standards.
Gives multiple concrete signs that correctness, reliability, and bounded behavior are central to how the applicant engineers security tooling.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how well the letter substantiates claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, named systems, counts, or technical detail.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures the depth and centrality of Go in the applicant's real production backend work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter explains the concrete effects, outcomes, or operational consequences of the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Lists responsibilities or technologies without explaining what changed because of the work.
Suggests benefit, but the outcome remains vague or implied.
Gives a clear before-and-after or operational result, such as a queue becoming routed, a bottleneck disappearing, or hours being saved.
Shows strong leverage-oriented impact articulation, tying the work to measurable capacity, broad downstream benefit, or a transformed operating model.

features.name: Maintainer mindset
features.description: Captures a bias toward operability, reliability, maintenance, and long-term care of systems rather than feature delivery alone.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Captures the overall distinctiveness, voice, and coherence of the letter as a persuasive narrative, separate from surface correctness.

levels.descriptor: Reads as flat, list-like, or heavily templated prose.
Is competent and readable, but largely generic in voice.
Has a noticeable hook, framing device, or coherent personal story.
Has a strong, memorable voice that reinforces fit without sacrificing substance.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-oriented security practice outside routine software engineering work, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public or upstream codebases, from fixing dependencies at the source to maintaining projects used by others.

levels.descriptor: No open-source work is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional patches or fixes sent upstream.
The letter shows regular contribution or maintainership, including review or release responsibilities.
The letter shows stewardship of a broadly used project or community, with clear responsibility for releases, roadmap, or contributor management.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, substance, and seriousness of self-directed engineering work outside formal job duties.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation toward foundational infrastructure or shared systems work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Programming language breadth
features.description: Captures the range of programming languages the applicant presents beyond the role's core language requirements.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how deeply and convincingly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Relevant production software experience
features.description: Captures the amount and maturity of professional experience building, launching, maintaining, and operating production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: Captures how specifically and convincingly the letter connects the applicant's background, motivation, and trajectory to this exact role and its stated requirements.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in the company or job title with little role-specific reasoning.
Shows some relevant interest, but the motivation remains broad or interchangeable.
Clearly ties motivation to security engineering, developer enablement, or backend tooling.
Gives nuanced and convincing motivation tightly tied to this team's charter and responsibilities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience performing structured security reviews, threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, code review, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures whether the letter understands the role as scaling security work through automation, triage systems, and high-leverage platform tooling rather than generic software engineering.

levels.descriptor: Interest in the role is generic and could fit many software jobs.
The letter shows some interest in security or backend impact, but the motivation stays broad.
The letter clearly wants to make secure behavior easier by default or reduce repetitive security toil.
The letter offers a nuanced philosophy of security automation as leverage, capacity creation, or quiet resilience.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the strength and relevance of formal external security certifications or credentialing cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or equivalent fundamentals.
Mentions a demanding practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter conveys a thoughtful security-engineering worldview or identity, beyond merely adjacent software experience.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: System ownership seniority
features.description: Captures the level of autonomy and end-to-end responsibility the applicant claims over the systems or security work they describe.

levels.descriptor: The letter mostly lists exposure, participation, or learning, with little evidence of ownership.
The letter shows implementation responsibility for individual components or tools.
The letter shows end-to-end ownership of services, tooling, or automations.
The letter shows architectural or design leadership over systems that set constraints or workflows for other engineers.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, deduplication, routing, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the surface correctness and professionalism of the prose, including spelling, grammar, proofreading, and copyediting quality.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures how strongly the applicant frames security engineering as enabling other developers rather than policing them.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not discuss the developers or teams who will use the tooling.
The letter shows a general desire to help teams, but not much detail about workflow impact.
The letter explicitly focuses on removing friction and making the secure path easier for engineers.
The letter consistently centers adoption, workflow fit, and secure-by-default behavior for busy developer teams.
